subject: science
passage: Ice cores drilled from the Antarctic ice sheet contain tiny bubbles of air that were sealed off as layers of old snow were slowly compressed into ice. Because each bubble preserves a sample of the atmosphere from the time it closed, the deepest cores allow scientists to measure carbon dioxide levels from roughly 800,000 years ago. The record from those ancient bubbles and the much younger ones above ______ that carbon dioxide levels today are higher than at any point in that long span.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the last sentence is "The record from those ancient bubbles and the much younger ones above them," and its verb is "shows." Even when a subject is long, no punctuation goes between the subject and its verb.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses, but it would split the subject from its verb "shows."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A single comma can't separate a subject from its verb, no matter how long the subject is.
explanation.C: Correct. No punctuation separates the long subject from its verb "shows."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A dash can't separate the subject from its verb "shows"; nothing here is being set off.
